candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — patient antibiotic-use education
candidate.educational_objective: Teach clients to use antibiotics exactly as prescribed, avoid sharing or saving leftover antibiotics, and seek professional guidance rather than independently shortening, extending, or reusing antimicrobial therapy.

options.A: I will take the antibiotic exactly as prescribed, will not share it or save leftover doses for another illness, and will contact my healthcare professional if I have questions or adverse effects.
options.B: I should stop the antibiotic on my own as soon as I feel better, even if the prescription instructions say to continue it.
options.C: I can save unused antibiotics for the next time I develop similar symptoms because this reduces unnecessary clinic visits.
options.D: If a family member develops similar symptoms, sharing my antibiotic is appropriate as long as we take the same dose.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. CDC's current antibiotic-use guidance advises clients to take antibiotics exactly as prescribed, not share them, not save them for later, and discuss questions or side effects with a healthcare professional. This wording is more accurate than a blanket instruction to 'finish every course no matter what,' because the prescribed duration itself may be changed by the treating clinician when clinically appropriate. B substitutes the client's own decision for the prescription. C and D can delay correct diagnosis and expose others to ineffective or harmful treatment.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Safe patient-level antibiotic stewardship means taking antibiotics according to current prescription instructions, not sharing or saving them, and involving the healthcare professional in treatment changes rather than self-modifying therapy.
candidate.source_document_title: Healthy Habits: Antibiotic Do's and Don'ts; Antibiotic Use and Antimicrobial Resistance Facts
candidate.source_locator: Healthy Habits — 'Take antibiotics exactly as prescribed': take them exactly as prescribed; do not share antibiotics; do not save them for later; do not take antibiotics prescribed for someone else; contact a healthcare professional with questions. Antibiotic Use and Antimicrobial Resistance Facts — misuse includes taking the wrong antibiotic, wrong dose, or antibiotic for the wrong length of time; appropriate use is necessary to reduce harm and antimicrobial-resistance pressure.
